renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_consensus_upset
  title: Replicate overlap of consensus peaks
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of replicates and counts the merged consensus intervals that every replicate of the combination called a peak on. It answers how reproducible the peak set is between replicates.
    How to read: a tall bar for all replicates together means the peaks are reproducible. Tall bars for single replicates mean that replicate calls peaks the others miss, which is typical of a noisy or over-sensitive library. Compare the set sizes on the left with the intersections.
    Note: SEACR publishes no minimum number of replicates, and the pipeline decides which consensus peaks to keep with its own replicate threshold.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_consensus_track
  title: Consensus intervals along the genome
  description: |-
    Each mark is a merged consensus interval on its chromosome, coloured by target and high according to the strongest maximum signal among the peaks merged into it. It answers where the replicates agree and how strong the signal is there.
    How to read: clusters of tall intervals are enriched domains, and an isolated tall interval is a candidate site. Compare targets to see which regions they share. Brush a region to filter the tiles of the tab.
    Lines and annotations: the line is the 95th percentile of the maximum signal in the table, a data-defined reference computed from the rows on show and not a SEACR cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Maximum signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: start
    score: max_signal
    feature: peak_id
    end: end
    category: target

- component: figure
  id: seacr_consensus_width_hist
  title: Consensus interval width by replicate support
  description: |-
    Each box is a replicate support level: the spread of the widths of the consensus intervals that this many replicates called. It answers whether intervals confirmed by more replicates are wider or narrower.
    How to read: a box that moves up with support means reproducible calls are broader domains, as expected for a broad mark. Similar boxes mean width does not depend on support. Very wide outliers are merged neighbouring peaks.
    Note: no width cut-off is drawn, because SEACR defines none.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: support
    y: width
    color: support
    labels:
      support: Replicates calling the interval
      width: Interval width (bp)

- component: card
  title: Consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the consensus intervals in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. The extra figure is the number of targets. It answers how large each peak set is.
    How to read: a target with far fewer intervals than the others has a weaker or more selective peak set. Compare it with the peak counts of its replicates.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: target
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: intervals, by target

- component: card
  title: Replicates per interval
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean number of replicates that called a peak on a consensus interval, and the box shows its spread. It answers how reproducible the peaks are on average.
    How to read: a mean close to the number of replicates means most intervals are shared. A mean close to one means most peaks are private to one replicate.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: num_samples
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Intervals by replicate support
  description: |-
    Each unit is a consensus interval and the ring splits them by how many replicates called a peak on it. It answers how much of the peak set is confirmed by more than one replicate.
    How to read: a large share at the highest support is a reproducible peak set. A ring dominated by single replicates means the replicates disagree.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: support
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: support
  caption: intervals, by replicate support

- component: card
  title: Total signal of consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean total signal, the summed fragment coverage of the peaks merged into an interval, and the histogram shows how it is distributed. It answers how strong the consensus intervals are.
    How to read: signal is strongly skewed, so the median sits well below the mean. A long right tail is a few very strong domains. SEACR gives no cut-off for the total signal.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: total_signal
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean, with the distribution

- component: table
  title: Consensus peak table
  description: |-
    Each row is a merged consensus interval with its target, caller, coordinates, width, replicates, signals and one 0 or 1 column per replicate. It answers which intervals are shared and how strong they are.
    How to read: sort by replicates to list the confirmed peaks, and by signal to list the strongest. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_class_stack
  title: Nucleosome classes per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the share of its fragments in each length class: sub-nucleosomal, mono-, di- and multi-nucleosomal. It answers how much of the library is nucleosome-free against nucleosome-bound.
    How to read: a sharp mark gives a sub-nucleosomal heavy library, and a broad mark a mononucleosomal heavy one, so replicates of one target should look alike. A library dominated by multi-nucleosomal fragments was digested too little.
    Lines and annotations: the classes are cut at 120, 250 and 450 bp. The 120 bp boundary follows the transcription factor sized fragments of the CUT&RUN paper, while 250 and 450 bp are this table's own bins and not a published cut-off.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: fraction
    color: fragment_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      fraction: Share of fragments
      fragment_class: Fragment class

- component: card
  title: Fragments counted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. It answers how much data each target contributes.
    How to read: targets with far fewer fragments have less depth, so their class shares are noisier. The extra figures are the median and largest class count.
  column: n_fragments
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Median fragment length per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median fragment length, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers where the typical fragment sits.
    How to read: histone marks sit near a nucleosome, about 180 bp, and a median far above it points to little digestion. Transcription factors push the median down with short fragments.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: sample_median_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mononucleosomal median length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the median length of the mononucleosomal fragments, between 120 and 250 bp (this table's own class), and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the nucleosome peak sits where it should.
    How to read: a value near 180 bp, the nucleosomal fragment length the nf-core/cutandrun docs give for histone marks, is a clean nucleosome peak. A value pushed to the edge of the class suggests the digestion is uneven.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: median_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('fragment_class') == 'Mononucleosomal'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mononucleosome to sub-nucleosome ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the ratio of mononucleosomal to sub-nucleosomal fragments, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the libraries are nucleosome-bound or nucleosome-free.
    How to read: a high ratio belongs to broad histone marks and a low one to sharp marks and transcription factors. Replicates of one target should have similar ratios, and a stray one is worth a look.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  column: mono_to_sub
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Fragment class table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a length class, with the fragments in it, their share, the median length inside the class and the sample-level ratio. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: sort by share to find the dominant class of each sample, and filter on a class to compare samples.

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_curve
  title: Fragment length distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the share of its fragments at every length, coloured by target. It answers whether the experiment cut around nucleosomes.
    How to read: a working experiment shows a nucleosome shoulder, about 150 to 180 bp, and for sharp marks or transcription factors a peak of short fragments below about 120 bp. A flat, featureless curve is a failed digestion. Replicates of one target should overlap.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_length
    y: fraction
    color: target
    line_group: sample
    labels:
      fragment_length: Fragment length (bp)
      fraction: Share of fragments
      target: Target

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_cumulative
  title: Cumulative fragment length
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the share of its fragments that are at most as long as the length on the horizontal axis, coloured by target. It answers how much of the library is short and how fast it fills up.
    How to read: a steep early rise means many short fragments and a late rise means long, poorly digested chromatin. Replicates that diverge differ in digestion. Read the value at 120 bp for the sub-nucleosomal share.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_length
    y: cumulative_fraction
    color: target
    line_group: sample
    labels:
      fragment_length: Fragment length (bp)
      cumulative_fraction: Cumulative share of fragments
      target: Target

- component: card
  title: Fragments counted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. The extra figure is the largest count at one length. It answers how much data each target contributes.
    How to read: a target with far fewer fragments has less depth, so its length curve is noisier.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Highest share at one length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest share of fragments at any single length and the histogram shows how the shares are distributed over all lengths and samples. It answers how sharp the length peak is.
    How to read: a high maximum means a sharp peak, as for a transcription factor. A low maximum with a wide spread is broad chromatin.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  column: fraction
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: highest share at one length, with the distribution

- component: card
  title: Samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples with a fragment histogram and the bars rank the targets by how many samples they hold. The extra figure counts the length rows. It answers how many libraries the curves are drawn from.
    How to read: targets with one sample cannot show replicate agreement.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by target

- component: table
  title: Fragment length table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a fragment length, with the count, its share and the share at most that long. It answers the exact numbers behind the curves.
    How to read: filter on a sample and sort by count to find its dominant lengths.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: frags_pileup_matrix
  title: Fragment pile-up around peak summits
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the strongest SEACR regions of a sample, each column a 100 bp bin around its summit, and the colour is the fragment coverage per million fragments of the sample. It answers whether the calls stand on a clean, centred pile-up.
    How to read: a bright vertical band at the centre means the signal is centred on the summit. A target with sharp peaks, such as a promoter mark, gives a narrow band, and a broad mark a wide one. Rows that are bright everywhere are broad domains.
    Lines and annotations: the marker at offset 0 is the summit of the region, the midpoint of its maximum signal interval as reported by SEACR. The window, 3 kb each side of it, is a fixed choice of this catalog's recipe, and rows are ordered by total signal.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: signal_matrix
  config:
    reference_label: Peak summit
  roles:
    region_id: peak_id
    position: offset_bp
    value: cpm
    group: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: frags_pileup_track
  title: Fragment coverage track
  description: |-
    Each bar is a 100 bp bin at its genomic position, with its fragment coverage per million fragments, coloured by target. It answers where along a locus the fragments pile up in each sample.
    How to read: peaks that are present in the replicates of one target and absent in the other target are specific to it. Only bins around the strongest calls are drawn, so empty stretches mean no strong call, not no signal.
    Note: the window around each call is the pipeline's own choice, and no signal threshold is drawn.
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: category
  roles:
    chromosome: chr
    position: bin_start
    value: cpm
    end: bin_end
    sample: sample
    category: target

- component: card
  title: Highest fragment coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest coverage per million fragments in any bin and the bars rank the targets by their highest bin. It answers which target has the sharpest pile-up.
    How to read: sharp marks give high, narrow maxima and broad marks give low ones, so compare within a target.
  column: cpm
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: highest bin, by target

- component: card
  title: Fragments in the windows
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in the windows around the strongest calls and the bars rank the targets by it. It answers how much of the library sits in the strongest regions.
    How to read: a target with few fragments in its windows has weaker calls. This is a count inside the windows, not a fraction of reads in peaks.
  column: fragments
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Coverage per bin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median coverage per million fragments over the bins of the windows, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how high the typical bin is.
    How to read: a low median with a high maximum is a sharp peak on a quiet background, and a high median is a broad domain.
  column: cpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Fragment pile-up table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, a peak and a 100 bp bin around its summit, with the fragments and the coverage per million in it. It answers the exact numbers behind the matrix and the track.
    How to read: filter on a peak and sort by offset to read its profile.

- component: figure
  id: seacr_summary_bar
  title: Regions called per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: the number of enriched regions SEACR called in it. It answers how many peaks each library yields.
    How to read: replicates of one target should be close, and a very different count is a sign of a depth or quality problem. A sharp mark calls few, wide regions and a broad mark many.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median number of regions per sample of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of SEACR. The count depends on the threshold mode and on the control.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31300027/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: num_peaks
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      num_peaks: Regions called
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: num_peaks

- component: card
  title: Regions called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of regions called over the samples in view and the histogram shows how the samples spread. The extra figures are the median and largest sample. It answers how many peaks the run produced.
    How to read: a single sample far from the rest has a different depth or a different target. Open the bar chart for the individual samples.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: num_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: regions, with the spread of samples
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Median region width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median region width in bases, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how broad the calls are.
    How to read: narrow regions, about a kilobase or less, fit promoter and transcription factor marks. Kilobase wide regions fit broad histone marks.
  column: width_median
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Bases covered by regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of bases covered by the called regions over the samples in view, and the histogram shows how the samples spread. It answers how much of the genome the calls cover.
    How to read: broad marks cover far more of the genome than sharp ones. Replicates of a target should cover similar amounts.
  column: total_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: bases covered, with the spread of samples

- component: card
  title: Coverage per base inside regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean over samples of the median fragment coverage per base inside their regions, and the histogram shows how samples spread. It answers how strong the signal inside the calls is.
    How to read: SEACR writes no FRiP score, so the coverage inside the calls is the signal to noise proxy. A target that worked carries far more than an IgG control taken through the same thresholding.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: signal_density_median
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean coverage per base, with the spread of samples

- component: table
  title: Peak summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its threshold mode, the regions called, the bases they cover and the width and signal statistics. It answers the quality of each library in numbers.
    How to read: compare replicates of one target row by row, and compare targets with the IgG control where there is one.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_signal
  title: Peak signal along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a SEACR region at the position of its summit, with the base 10 logarithm of its total fragment coverage on the vertical axis. It answers where in the genome the strongest signal sits.
    How to read: tall points mark strong enriched domains and clusters of them mark broad regions. A level, dense band means weak calls that all sit close to the threshold. Use the track view to read individual loci.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the scores in the table, a data-defined reference and not a SEACR cut-off. SEACR gives no significance for a region, since it reports coverage and not a p-value.
    Note: with tens of thousands of calls per sample the points overplot, so read the clusters rather than single points.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: log10 total signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: summit
    score: log10_total_signal
    feature: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_track
  title: Peak calls along the genome
  description: |-
    Each mark is a SEACR region drawn as the interval it covers, coloured by sample and high according to the logarithm of its total fragment coverage. It answers where each sample has enriched regions and how strong they are.
    How to read: regions shared by the replicates of a target are reproducible candidates, and a region seen in only one sample needs checking. Brush a locus to filter the tiles of the tab.
    Lines and annotations: the line is the 95th percentile of the scores in the table, a data-defined reference computed from the rows on show and not a SEACR cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: log10 total signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: start
    score: log10_total_signal
    feature: peak_id
    end: end
    category: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_coverage
  title: Peak signal track
  description: |-
    Each bar is a SEACR region at its coordinates, high according to the logarithm of its total fragment coverage and coloured by sample. It answers how the calls of the samples line up at a locus.
    How to read: matching bars in the replicates of a target are a reproducible peak, and a bar in only one sample is a private call. Compare targets to find specific regions.
    Note: no signal threshold is drawn, because SEACR defines none.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chr
    position: start
    value: log10_total_signal
    end: end
    sample: sample

- component: figure
  id: seacr_signal_scatter
  title: Total against maximum signal
  description: |-
    Each point is a region: its total fragment coverage against the highest coverage inside it, on logarithmic axes and coloured by sample. It answers whether strong regions are strong because they are tall or because they are wide.
    How to read: the points rise together, and a region far below the trend is wide and flat, such as a broad domain. A region far above it is a narrow spike. Compare samples to see which has the taller peaks.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: total_signal
    y: max_signal
    color: sample
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    labels:
      total_signal: Total signal
      max_signal: Maximum signal
      sample: Sample

- component: figure
  id: seacr_width_hist
  title: Region width per sample
  description: |-
    Each box is a sample: the spread of the widths of its regions in bases, on a logarithmic axis. It answers how broad the calls of each sample are.
    How to read: sharp marks give narrow regions and broad marks wide ones, so replicates of one target should look alike. A sample with a very different box has a different threshold or depth.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median region width of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of SEACR.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: width
    color: sample
    log_y: true
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      width: Region width (bp)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: width

- component: card
  title: Regions called
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the regions in view and the ring splits them by sample. The extra figure is the number of samples. It answers how the calls are shared between libraries.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one sample means that sample calls far more regions, usually a broad mark or a deeper library.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: sample
  caption: regions, by sample

- component: card
  title: Median region width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median region width in bases and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how broad the calls are.
    How to read: narrow regions fit sharp marks and wide ones broad marks. A long upper whisker is merged neighbouring signal blocks.
  column: width
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Total signal in regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the summed fragment coverage inside all regions in view and the histogram shows how it is distributed over the regions. It answers how much signal the calls hold.
    How to read: signal is strongly skewed, so a few regions carry most of it. The extra figures are the median and the strongest region.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: total_signal
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: total, with the distribution of regions

- component: card
  title: Coverage per base
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fragment coverage per base inside a region and the histogram shows how it is distributed. It answers how dense the signal is.
    How to read: a target that worked has much more coverage per base than an IgG control. Compare it between samples and replicates.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: signal_density
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean, with the distribution of regions

- component: table
  title: Peak call table
  description: |-
    Each row is a SEACR region with its sample, coordinates, width, summit, total and maximum signal and coverage per base. It answers the exact numbers behind the tiles.
    How to read: sort by total signal to list the strongest regions. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_consensus_upset
  title: Replicate overlap of consensus peaks
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of replicates and counts the merged consensus intervals that every replicate of the combination called a peak on. It answers how reproducible the peak set is between replicates.
    How to read: a tall bar for all replicates together means the peaks are reproducible. Tall bars for single replicates mean that replicate calls peaks the others miss, which is typical of a noisy or over-sensitive library. Compare the set sizes on the left with the intersections.
    Note: SEACR publishes no minimum number of replicates, and the pipeline decides which consensus peaks to keep with its own replicate threshold.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_consensus_track
  title: Consensus intervals along the genome
  description: |-
    Each mark is a merged consensus interval on its chromosome, coloured by target and high according to the strongest maximum signal among the peaks merged into it. It answers where the replicates agree and how strong the signal is there.
    How to read: clusters of tall intervals are enriched domains, and an isolated tall interval is a candidate site. Compare targets to see which regions they share. Brush a region to filter the tiles of the tab.
    Lines and annotations: the line is the 95th percentile of the maximum signal in the table, a data-defined reference computed from the rows on show and not a SEACR cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Maximum signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: start
    score: max_signal
    feature: peak_id
    end: end
    category: target

- component: figure
  id: seacr_consensus_width_hist
  title: Consensus interval width by replicate support
  description: |-
    Each box is a replicate support level: the spread of the widths of the consensus intervals that this many replicates called. It answers whether intervals confirmed by more replicates are wider or narrower.
    How to read: a box that moves up with support means reproducible calls are broader domains, as expected for a broad mark. Similar boxes mean width does not depend on support. Very wide outliers are merged neighbouring peaks.
    Note: no width cut-off is drawn, because SEACR defines none.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: support
    y: width
    color: support
    labels:
      support: Replicates calling the interval
      width: Interval width (bp)

- component: card
  title: Consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the consensus intervals in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. The extra figure is the number of targets. It answers how large each peak set is.
    How to read: a target with far fewer intervals than the others has a weaker or more selective peak set. Compare it with the peak counts of its replicates.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: target
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: intervals, by target

- component: card
  title: Replicates per interval
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean number of replicates that called a peak on a consensus interval, and the box shows its spread. It answers how reproducible the peaks are on average.
    How to read: a mean close to the number of replicates means most intervals are shared. A mean close to one means most peaks are private to one replicate.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: num_samples
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Intervals by replicate support
  description: |-
    Each unit is a consensus interval and the ring splits them by how many replicates called a peak on it. It answers how much of the peak set is confirmed by more than one replicate.
    How to read: a large share at the highest support is a reproducible peak set. A ring dominated by single replicates means the replicates disagree.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: support
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: support
  caption: intervals, by replicate support

- component: card
  title: Total signal of consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean total signal, the summed fragment coverage of the peaks merged into an interval, and the histogram shows how it is distributed. It answers how strong the consensus intervals are.
    How to read: signal is strongly skewed, so the median sits well below the mean. A long right tail is a few very strong domains. SEACR gives no cut-off for the total signal.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: total_signal
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean, with the distribution

- component: table
  title: Consensus peak table
  description: |-
    Each row is a merged consensus interval with its target, caller, coordinates, width, replicates, signals and one 0 or 1 column per replicate. It answers which intervals are shared and how strong they are.
    How to read: sort by replicates to list the confirmed peaks, and by signal to list the strongest. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_class_stack
  title: Nucleosome classes per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the share of its fragments in each length class: sub-nucleosomal, mono-, di- and multi-nucleosomal. It answers how much of the library is nucleosome-free against nucleosome-bound.
    How to read: a sharp mark gives a sub-nucleosomal heavy library, and a broad mark a mononucleosomal heavy one, so replicates of one target should look alike. A library dominated by multi-nucleosomal fragments was digested too little.
    Lines and annotations: the classes are cut at 120, 250 and 450 bp. The 120 bp boundary follows the transcription factor sized fragments of the CUT&RUN paper, while 250 and 450 bp are this table's own bins and not a published cut-off.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: fraction
    color: fragment_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      fraction: Share of fragments
      fragment_class: Fragment class

- component: card
  title: Fragments counted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. It answers how much data each target contributes.
    How to read: targets with far fewer fragments have less depth, so their class shares are noisier. The extra figures are the median and largest class count.
  column: n_fragments
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Median fragment length per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median fragment length, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers where the typical fragment sits.
    How to read: histone marks sit near a nucleosome, about 180 bp, and a median far above it points to little digestion. Transcription factors push the median down with short fragments.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: sample_median_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mononucleosomal median length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the median length of the mononucleosomal fragments, between 120 and 250 bp (this table's own class), and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the nucleosome peak sits where it should.
    How to read: a value near 180 bp, the nucleosomal fragment length the nf-core/cutandrun docs give for histone marks, is a clean nucleosome peak. A value pushed to the edge of the class suggests the digestion is uneven.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: median_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('fragment_class') == 'Mononucleosomal'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mononucleosome to sub-nucleosome ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the ratio of mononucleosomal to sub-nucleosomal fragments, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the libraries are nucleosome-bound or nucleosome-free.
    How to read: a high ratio belongs to broad histone marks and a low one to sharp marks and transcription factors. Replicates of one target should have similar ratios, and a stray one is worth a look.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  column: mono_to_sub
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Fragment class table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a length class, with the fragments in it, their share, the median length inside the class and the sample-level ratio. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: sort by share to find the dominant class of each sample, and filter on a class to compare samples.

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_curve
  title: Fragment length distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the share of its fragments at every length, coloured by target. It answers whether the experiment cut around nucleosomes.
    How to read: a working experiment shows a nucleosome shoulder, about 150 to 180 bp, and for sharp marks or transcription factors a peak of short fragments below about 120 bp. A flat, featureless curve is a failed digestion. Replicates of one target should overlap.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_length
    y: fraction
    color: target
    line_group: sample
    labels:
      fragment_length: Fragment length (bp)
      fraction: Share of fragments
      target: Target

- component: figure
  id: seacr_fragment_cumulative
  title: Cumulative fragment length
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the share of its fragments that are at most as long as the length on the horizontal axis, coloured by target. It answers how much of the library is short and how fast it fills up.
    How to read: a steep early rise means many short fragments and a late rise means long, poorly digested chromatin. Replicates that diverge differ in digestion. Read the value at 120 bp for the sub-nucleosomal share.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_length
    y: cumulative_fraction
    color: target
    line_group: sample
    labels:
      fragment_length: Fragment length (bp)
      cumulative_fraction: Cumulative share of fragments
      target: Target

- component: card
  title: Fragments counted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in view and the bars rank the targets by how many they hold. The extra figure is the largest count at one length. It answers how much data each target contributes.
    How to read: a target with far fewer fragments has less depth, so its length curve is noisier.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Highest share at one length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest share of fragments at any single length and the histogram shows how the shares are distributed over all lengths and samples. It answers how sharp the length peak is.
    How to read: a high maximum means a sharp peak, as for a transcription factor. A low maximum with a wide spread is broad chromatin.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28079019/
  column: fraction
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: highest share at one length, with the distribution

- component: card
  title: Samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples with a fragment histogram and the bars rank the targets by how many samples they hold. The extra figure counts the length rows. It answers how many libraries the curves are drawn from.
    How to read: targets with one sample cannot show replicate agreement.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by target

- component: table
  title: Fragment length table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a fragment length, with the count, its share and the share at most that long. It answers the exact numbers behind the curves.
    How to read: filter on a sample and sort by count to find its dominant lengths.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: frags_pileup_matrix
  title: Fragment pile-up around peak summits
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the strongest SEACR regions of a sample, each column a 100 bp bin around its summit, and the colour is the fragment coverage per million fragments of the sample. It answers whether the calls stand on a clean, centred pile-up.
    How to read: a bright vertical band at the centre means the signal is centred on the summit. A target with sharp peaks, such as a promoter mark, gives a narrow band, and a broad mark a wide one. Rows that are bright everywhere are broad domains.
    Lines and annotations: the marker at offset 0 is the summit of the region, the midpoint of its maximum signal interval as reported by SEACR. The window, 3 kb each side of it, is a fixed choice of this catalog's recipe, and rows are ordered by total signal.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: signal_matrix
  config:
    reference_label: Peak summit
  roles:
    region_id: peak_id
    position: offset_bp
    value: cpm
    group: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: frags_pileup_track
  title: Fragment coverage track
  description: |-
    Each bar is a 100 bp bin at its genomic position, with its fragment coverage per million fragments, coloured by target. It answers where along a locus the fragments pile up in each sample.
    How to read: peaks that are present in the replicates of one target and absent in the other target are specific to it. Only bins around the strongest calls are drawn, so empty stretches mean no strong call, not no signal.
    Note: the window around each call is the pipeline's own choice, and no signal threshold is drawn.
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: category
  roles:
    chromosome: chr
    position: bin_start
    value: cpm
    end: bin_end
    sample: sample
    category: target

- component: card
  title: Highest fragment coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest coverage per million fragments in any bin and the bars rank the targets by their highest bin. It answers which target has the sharpest pile-up.
    How to read: sharp marks give high, narrow maxima and broad marks give low ones, so compare within a target.
  column: cpm
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: highest bin, by target

- component: card
  title: Fragments in the windows
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of fragments in the windows around the strongest calls and the bars rank the targets by it. It answers how much of the library sits in the strongest regions.
    How to read: a target with few fragments in its windows has weaker calls. This is a count inside the windows, not a fraction of reads in peaks.
  column: fragments
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fragments, by target

- component: card
  title: Coverage per bin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median coverage per million fragments over the bins of the windows, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how high the typical bin is.
    How to read: a low median with a high maximum is a sharp peak on a quiet background, and a high median is a broad domain.
  column: cpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Fragment pile-up table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, a peak and a 100 bp bin around its summit, with the fragments and the coverage per million in it. It answers the exact numbers behind the matrix and the track.
    How to read: filter on a peak and sort by offset to read its profile.

- component: figure
  id: seacr_summary_bar
  title: Regions called per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: the number of enriched regions SEACR called in it. It answers how many peaks each library yields.
    How to read: replicates of one target should be close, and a very different count is a sign of a depth or quality problem. A sharp mark calls few, wide regions and a broad mark many.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median number of regions per sample of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of SEACR. The count depends on the threshold mode and on the control.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31300027/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: num_peaks
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      num_peaks: Regions called
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: num_peaks

- component: card
  title: Regions called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of regions called over the samples in view and the histogram shows how the samples spread. The extra figures are the median and largest sample. It answers how many peaks the run produced.
    How to read: a single sample far from the rest has a different depth or a different target. Open the bar chart for the individual samples.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: num_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: regions, with the spread of samples
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Median region width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median region width in bases, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how broad the calls are.
    How to read: narrow regions, about a kilobase or less, fit promoter and transcription factor marks. Kilobase wide regions fit broad histone marks.
  column: width_median
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Bases covered by regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of bases covered by the called regions over the samples in view, and the histogram shows how the samples spread. It answers how much of the genome the calls cover.
    How to read: broad marks cover far more of the genome than sharp ones. Replicates of a target should cover similar amounts.
  column: total_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: bases covered, with the spread of samples

- component: card
  title: Coverage per base inside regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean over samples of the median fragment coverage per base inside their regions, and the histogram shows how samples spread. It answers how strong the signal inside the calls is.
    How to read: SEACR writes no FRiP score, so the coverage inside the calls is the signal to noise proxy. A target that worked carries far more than an IgG control taken through the same thresholding.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: signal_density_median
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean coverage per base, with the spread of samples

- component: table
  title: Peak summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its threshold mode, the regions called, the bases they cover and the width and signal statistics. It answers the quality of each library in numbers.
    How to read: compare replicates of one target row by row, and compare targets with the IgG control where there is one.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_signal
  title: Peak signal along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a SEACR region at the position of its summit, with the base 10 logarithm of its total fragment coverage on the vertical axis. It answers where in the genome the strongest signal sits.
    How to read: tall points mark strong enriched domains and clusters of them mark broad regions. A level, dense band means weak calls that all sit close to the threshold. Use the track view to read individual loci.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the scores in the table, a data-defined reference and not a SEACR cut-off. SEACR gives no significance for a region, since it reports coverage and not a p-value.
    Note: with tens of thousands of calls per sample the points overplot, so read the clusters rather than single points.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: log10 total signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: summit
    score: log10_total_signal
    feature: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_track
  title: Peak calls along the genome
  description: |-
    Each mark is a SEACR region drawn as the interval it covers, coloured by sample and high according to the logarithm of its total fragment coverage. It answers where each sample has enriched regions and how strong they are.
    How to read: regions shared by the replicates of a target are reproducible candidates, and a region seen in only one sample needs checking. Brush a locus to filter the tiles of the tab.
    Lines and annotations: the line is the 95th percentile of the scores in the table, a data-defined reference computed from the rows on show and not a SEACR cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: log10 total signal
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: start
    score: log10_total_signal
    feature: peak_id
    end: end
    category: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: seacr_peak_coverage
  title: Peak signal track
  description: |-
    Each bar is a SEACR region at its coordinates, high according to the logarithm of its total fragment coverage and coloured by sample. It answers how the calls of the samples line up at a locus.
    How to read: matching bars in the replicates of a target are a reproducible peak, and a bar in only one sample is a private call. Compare targets to find specific regions.
    Note: no signal threshold is drawn, because SEACR defines none.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chr
    position: start
    value: log10_total_signal
    end: end
    sample: sample

- component: figure
  id: seacr_signal_scatter
  title: Total against maximum signal
  description: |-
    Each point is a region: its total fragment coverage against the highest coverage inside it, on logarithmic axes and coloured by sample. It answers whether strong regions are strong because they are tall or because they are wide.
    How to read: the points rise together, and a region far below the trend is wide and flat, such as a broad domain. A region far above it is a narrow spike. Compare samples to see which has the taller peaks.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: total_signal
    y: max_signal
    color: sample
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    labels:
      total_signal: Total signal
      max_signal: Maximum signal
      sample: Sample

- component: figure
  id: seacr_width_hist
  title: Region width per sample
  description: |-
    Each box is a sample: the spread of the widths of its regions in bases, on a logarithmic axis. It answers how broad the calls of each sample are.
    How to read: sharp marks give narrow regions and broad marks wide ones, so replicates of one target should look alike. A sample with a very different box has a different threshold or depth.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median region width of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of SEACR.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: width
    color: sample
    log_y: true
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      width: Region width (bp)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: width

- component: card
  title: Regions called
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the regions in view and the ring splits them by sample. The extra figure is the number of samples. It answers how the calls are shared between libraries.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one sample means that sample calls far more regions, usually a broad mark or a deeper library.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: sample
  caption: regions, by sample

- component: card
  title: Median region width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median region width in bases and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how broad the calls are.
    How to read: narrow regions fit sharp marks and wide ones broad marks. A long upper whisker is merged neighbouring signal blocks.
  column: width
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Total signal in regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the summed fragment coverage inside all regions in view and the histogram shows how it is distributed over the regions. It answers how much signal the calls hold.
    How to read: signal is strongly skewed, so a few regions carry most of it. The extra figures are the median and the strongest region.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: total_signal
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: total, with the distribution of regions

- component: card
  title: Coverage per base
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fragment coverage per base inside a region and the histogram shows how it is distributed. It answers how dense the signal is.
    How to read: a target that worked has much more coverage per base than an IgG control. Compare it between samples and replicates.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FredHutch/SEACR/master/README.md
  column: signal_density
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean, with the distribution of regions

- component: table
  title: Peak call table
  description: |-
    Each row is a SEACR region with its sample, coordinates, width, summit, total and maximum signal and coverage per base. It answers the exact numbers behind the tiles.
    How to read: sort by total signal to list the strongest regions. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id
